question.prompt: Each of a group of \(50\) girls is blonde or brunette and is blue-eyed or brown-eyed. If \(14\) are blue-eyed blondes, \(31\) are brunettes, and \(18\) are brown-eyed, then the number of brown-eyed brunettes is:

solutions.explanation:
The hair-color categories divide all \(50\) girls into two separate groups. Since \(31\) are brunettes, the number of blondes is
\[50-31=19.\]
Of these blondes, \(14\) are blue-eyed, so \(19-14=5\) are brown-eyed.

Every brown-eyed girl is either blonde or brunette, and belongs to exactly one of those groups. Therefore the number of brown-eyed brunettes is
\[18-5=\boxed{13},\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Find the missing groups by subtraction
